briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate briefing for July 27, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensifying Climate Crisis: Global Heatwaves and Wildfire Spread
sections.content: Today, severe signs of the global climate crisis have been reported. In the United States, 70 million people were affected by 49℃ heatwaves due to the third 'heat dome' phenomenon in July alone [24]. Canada and Europe also experienced consecutive large-scale wildfires and heat domes, leading to the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people [3, 17, 137, 161]. Domestically, the start of heatwaves has accelerated by a month, and tropical nights have tripled, making longer summers a common occurrence [25, 26]. In Gyeongnam Province, the estimated number of heat-related deaths increased to 3, prompting the issuance of a severe heatwave alert [126]. Climate change is causing irregular outbreaks of anthracnose in fruit trees in the agricultural sector [5], posing new threats to the UNESCO rice terraces in the Philippines [128], and a warning has been issued that it could cause an additional 430,000 deaths annually by 2050 [143]. Cities are unprepared for such extreme weather, endangering the homeless in London, and raising concerns that plague outbreaks could become a new normal in New York [130, 162].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Change Adaptation and Agricultural Innovation Efforts
sections.content: Amidst this climate crisis, various regions are actively pursuing efforts to adapt to climate change. The Chungbuk Provincial Council urged a shift in agricultural policies to respond to climate change [1], while Anseong City and the Gyeongnam Agricultural Research & Extension Services are accelerating the development of heat-resistant waxy corn and summer apple varieties [7, 11, 14, 15, 21, 23]. Hamyang County is introducing temperature reduction technologies to prevent heatwave damage to floricultural crops [8], and Busan City is exploring strategies for marine resource management and co-prosperity in the fishing industry [16]. Diverse sectors are thus developing customized measures for climate change. Furthermore, the Gyeonggi Provincial Council is pushing for ordinance revisions to protect workers from heatwaves and cold waves [13], and the Korea Meteorological Administration is conducting campaigns to support vulnerable groups during heatwaves [19], demonstrating ongoing efforts to protect socially vulnerable populations.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating the Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Domestic efforts to transition to a carbon-neutral society are also being made in various ways. Chung-Ang University was selected for Seoul City's 'RISE 10 Challenge' and is embarking on long-term research for implementing an AI-based carbon-neutral city [27, 31, 34, 35, 45, 54, 62]. Namseoul University and Cheonan City are operating carbon-neutral expert training courses to spread a culture of practical action in local communities [28, 32, 36, 38, 40, 46, 49, 56, 60]. NH Nonghyup Bank purchased 5,254 tons of carbon credits from farmers, contributing to increased farm income and carbon neutrality [29, 47, 50, 53, 58, 59, 61, 63]. Various entities, including Saemaul leaders and daycare centers, are taking the lead in everyday carbon-neutral practices such as resource recycling, throwing EM soil balls, and installing green curtains [30, 48, 52]. In addition, the tidal flats of Chungnam are evolving into ecological infrastructure based on blue carbon [41], and Jung-gu is conducting greenhouse gas diagnostics and consultations [42], expanding nationwide efforts for carbon neutrality.

sections.title: ⚠️ Renewable Energy Target Achievement: Challenges and Policy Improvement Tasks
sections.content: Amidst the emphasis on the importance of renewable energy transition, a warning has been issued that Korea's 2030 target of 100 GW of renewable energy is facing a 'red light' [66, 73, 85, 86, 92, 114, 115]. The KDI pointed out that the pace of renewable energy deployment needs to be quadrupled from its current rate [66, 67, 87, 88, 89, 93, 98], emphasizing that expanding subsidies alone has limitations and that improvements in the power grid, capital procurement, and deployment support systems must be pursued concurrently [65, 72, 74, 75, 77, 80, 82, 83, 84, 91, 102, 106, 107, 108, 113, 116, 117, 120, 121, 125]. Meanwhile, renewable energy-related stocks collectively showed weakness due to factors such as falling international oil prices, revealing market instability [64, 71, 90, 103, 112, 122]. The Constitutional Court's decision of unconstitutionality regarding the Carbon Neutrality Basic Act, stating it does not sufficiently protect the fundamental rights of future generations, further highlighted the need for policy improvement [124].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Climate Action and New Environmental Regulations
sections.content: In the international community, the importance of corporate responsibility and the introduction of new technologies in responding to climate change are being highlighted. A French court ordered TotalEnergies to adapt its business to climate change, but TotalEnergies announced its intention to appeal [129, 138, 142]. Furthermore, new research has warned that climate change is reshaping renewable energy plans, and Africa needs to reconsider solar and wind investments [150]. Domestically, companies are continuing to invest in renewable energy, with Samsung C&T investing 50 billion KRW in Samsung Asset Management's renewable energy fund [94]. Korea Southern Power and Korea Western Power are contributing to improving energy efficiency by utilizing idle military sites for solar power generation and ESS construction [95, 96, 99, 100, 101, 104, 109, 123]. The government is also making efforts to secure sustainable energy sources, including initiating R&D for biomass solid fuel that utilizes livestock manure as renewable energy [119].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the challenges faced by nations worldwide amidst the intensifying climate crisis and the diverse efforts being made to overcome them. This concludes today's climate briefing.
